complete_source_units.text: In the second year under King Darius, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the Lord came through Haggai the prophet, saying: “Speak now to Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, from the tribe of Judah, and to Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, saying:
‘Thus says the Lord Almighty: These people say, “The time has not arrived to rebuild the house of the Lord.”’”
The word of the Lord came through Haggai the prophet, saying:
“Is it time for you to live in your houses with recessed ceilings, while this house has been laid waste?
And now, thus says the Lord Almighty: Set your hearts upon your ways.

You sowed much and brought in little; you ate, but were not satisfied; you drank, but not to intoxication; you clothed yourselves, but were not warmed in them. The one gathering wages gathered them into a bundle with holes.
Thus says the Lord Almighty: Place your hearts upon your ways.
Go up onto the mountain, cut wood and rebuild the house. I will take pleasure in it and be glorified, said the Lord.

You looked for much, and it came to little; it was brought into the house, and I blew it away. Therefore, thus says the Lord Almighty: Because My house is desolate, while each of you hurries to his own house,
therefore heaven will hold back dew, and the earth will withhold its produce.
I will bring a sword upon the land and the mountains, upon grain, wine and oil, and whatever the earth produces, upon people and livestock, and upon all the labors of their hands.”

Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, from the tribe of Judah, Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and all the remnant of the people listened to the voice of the Lord their God and the words of Haggai the prophet, as the Lord their God had sent him to them. The people feared before the Lord.
Haggai, the messenger of the Lord, said to the people, “I am with you, says the Lord.”

The Lord stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, from the tribe of Judah, the spirit of Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and the spirit of the remnant of all the people. They came in and were carrying out work on the house of the Lord Almighty, their God,
on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year under King Darius.
In the seventh month, on the twenty-first day of the month, the Lord spoke through Haggai the prophet, saying:
“Speak now to Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, from the tribe of Judah, to Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to all the remnant of the people, saying:
Who among you saw this house in its former glory? How do you see it now? As though it did not exist before you.

But now be strong, Zerubbabel, says the Lord; be strong, Joshua, son of Jehozadak, the high priest; let all the people of the land be strong, says the Lord, and work, for I am with you, says the Lord Almighty,
and My Spirit stands in your midst. Take courage.
For thus says the Lord Almighty: Once more I will shake heaven and earth, the sea and the dry land.
And I will shake all the nations, and the choice things of all the nations shall come; and I will fill this house with glory, says the Lord Almighty.
The silver is Mine and the gold is Mine, says the Lord Almighty.

For the latter glory of this house will be greater than the former, says the Lord Almighty; in this place I will give peace, says the Lord Almighty, and peace of soul as a possession for everyone building to raise this sanctuary.”
On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year under Darius, the word of the Lord came to Haggai the prophet, saying:
“Thus says the Lord Almighty: Ask the priests about the law, saying:
If someone takes holy meat in the edge of his garment and the edge of his garment touches bread, cooked food, wine, oil or any food, will it become holy?” The priests answered, “No.”
Haggai said, “If one defiled through a dead person touches any of these, will it be defiled?” The priests answered, “It will be defiled.”

Haggai answered, “So is this people, and so is this nation before Me, says the Lord; so are all the works of their hands, and whoever approaches there will be defiled because of their morning gains. They will suffer because of their labors, and you hated those who rebuked at the gates.
And now, please set your hearts on the time before this day, before stone was placed upon stone in the sanctuary of the Lord,
on how things were with you: when you put twenty sata of barley into a bin, there were ten sata of barley; when you went to the wine vat to draw fifty metretai, there were twenty.
I struck you with barrenness, damage from wind and hail—all the works of your hands—and you did not turn to Me, says the Lord.
Please direct your hearts from this day onward; from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month and from the day the sanctuary of the Lord was founded, put it in your hearts:
whether it will yet be recognized on the threshing floor, and whether the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate and the olive trees still bear no fruit. From this day I will bless.”
The word of the Lord came a second time to Haggai the prophet on the twenty-fourth day of the month, saying:
“Speak to Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, from the tribe of Judah, saying: I am shaking heaven and earth, the sea and the dry land,

and I will overturn the thrones of kings and destroy the strength of the kings of the nations. I will overturn chariots and riders; horses and their riders will fall, each with a sword against his brother.
On that day, says the Lord Almighty, I will take you, Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, My servant, says the Lord, and make you like a signet, for I have chosen you, says the Lord Almighty.”

The parallel named participants are retained with each text's spellings.

retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai reports the people's claim that the rebuilding time has not arrived; Ezra records that work on God's house stood idle until Darius's second year. The narrative supplies the prolonged stoppage to which Haggai's appeal speaks, without equating external force with the people's stated excuse.

retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai introduces the Lord's word through the named prophet; Ezra explicitly identifies Haggai as prophesying to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in God's name. This links the named prophetic ministry, rather than merely two anonymous revelation headings.

retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai challenges inhabitants of houses with recessed ceilings while God's house lies waste; David notices that he lives in a cedar house while God's ark remains in a tent. Both contrast domestic comfort with the condition of the divine dwelling, in different historical settings.

the king said to Nathan the prophet, “Look now, I dwell in a cedar house, while the ark of God remains inside the tent.”
Nathan said to the king, “Go and do all that is in your heart, for the Lord is with you.”

retained_full_triples.relationship: examination of one's way oriented toward the Lord
retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai commands the people to set their hearts on their ways; Lamentations describes the way being searched and examined and calls for return to the Lord. Both connect reflection on conduct with a response toward God.

target_units.text: Our way was searched and examined; let us return to the Lord.

retained_full_triples.relationship: much sowing but little harvest and frustrated crop enjoyment
retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai describes much sowing with little brought in and unsatisfied consumption; Deuteronomy's curse describes much seed with little gathered and denied enjoyment of wine and oil. The connection concerns agricultural futility, without assigning Deuteronomy's named pests to Haggai.

You shall plant a vineyard and dress it, but shall neither drink wine nor rejoice in it; for the worm shall devour it.
You shall have olive trees throughout all your borders, but shall not anoint yourself with oil; for your olives shall fall away.

retained_full_triples.relationship: eating without satisfaction as covenant affliction
retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai says the people ate without being satisfied; Leviticus warns of scarcity in which people eat and are not filled. Both treat food that fails to satisfy as an affliction.

retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai attributes the reduced yield to His desolate house while people hurry to their own houses; the earlier challenge contrasts their finished ceilings with His wasted house. The repeated contrast makes the reason for the shortfall explicit.

retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai announces heaven holding back dew; Elijah announces that no dew or rain will come apart from his prophetic word before the living Lord. Both make withheld dew an announced divine judgment, without equating the episodes.

retained_full_triples.relationship: the Lord bringing a sword as judgment
retained_full_triples.rationale: The native Haggai passage says the Lord brings a sword upon land, produce, people and labor; Leviticus warns that God brings a sword exacting covenant penalty. The correspondence preserves sword language rather than replacing Haggai's word with drought.

retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai asks those who saw the former glory how the present house appears; Ezra describes elders who saw the first house weeping as the new foundation is before them. Both make living memory of the first house important to the response to rebuilding.

retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai commands leaders and people to be strong and work because the Lord is with them; Joshua is commanded to be strong and courageous because the Lord is with him. The matching assurance undergirds action in each commission.

retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai tells the people and leaders to be strong and work; Zechariah tells hearers of the prophets at the founding and building of the temple to have strong hands. Both encourage the rebuilding community's labor.

retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai assures the community that God's Spirit stands in their midst and calls for courage; Zechariah's word to Zerubbabel locates effectiveness in God's Spirit rather than great power or strength. The Spirit's presence or agency supports the work in both.

retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai promises once more to shake heaven and earth, sea and dry land; Hebrews quotes the promise to shake earth and heaven once more and reflects on the removal of shaken things. The explicit repeated wording establishes the citation relationship.

Now “yet once more” indicates the removal of the things shaken, as things that have been made, so that the things not shaken may remain.

retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai says the nations' choice things will come and His house will be filled with glory; Isaiah describes nations' wealth, gold and offerings arriving, followed by the glorification of God's house. The relationship follows the native plural choice things rather than substituting a singular personal title.

retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai declares silver and gold His; David acknowledges that everything given for God's house comes from God's own hand and belongs to Him. The surrounding temple donations include gold and silver, making the ownership statement materially specific.

retained_full_triples.relationship: priests charged to distinguish holiness and teach the law
retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai asks the priests for a legal ruling; Leviticus charges the priests to distinguish holy from profane and clean from unclean and teach the Lord's statutes. This explains their role in the following holiness questions.
retained_full_triples.source_text: “Thus says the Lord Almighty: Ask the priests about the law, saying:

target_units.text: to distinguish between the holy and the profane, and between the unclean and the clean.
And you shall instruct the sons of Israel in all the statutes which the Lord spoke unto them by the hand of Moses.

retained_full_triples.relationship: distinction between direct holy-flesh contact and indirect contact through a garment
retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai's priests deny that food becomes holy when touched by the garment edge carrying holy meat; Leviticus calls the sacrifice most holy and says one touching its flesh is sanctified. The comparison carefully distinguishes direct contact with flesh from the mediated contact asked about in Haggai.
retained_full_triples.source_text: If someone takes holy meat in the edge of his garment and the edge of his garment touches bread, cooked food, wine, oil or any food, will it become holy?” The priests answered, “No.”

The priest who offers it up shall eat it. It shall be eaten in a holy place, in the court of the Tent of Testimony.
Whosoever touches its flesh shall be sanctified; and if any of its blood is sprinkled upon a garment, what it was sprinkled upon shall be washed in a holy place.

retained_full_triples.relationship: corpse contact as a source of uncleanness
retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai asks about someone defiled through a dead person and the priests affirm resulting defilement on touch; Numbers says touching a dead person makes one unclean and explains the need for purification. This supplies the legal basis of the person's condition.
retained_full_triples.source_text: Haggai said, “If one defiled through a dead person touches any of these, will it be defiled?” The priests answered, “It will be defiled.”

target_units.text: Whosoever touches a dead person, any human being who has died, shall be unclean for seven days.
That person shall be purified on the third day and on the seventh day, and he shall be clean. If he is not purified on the third day and on the seventh day, he shall not be clean.

Whosoever touches the dead body of any human being who has died, and is not purified, has defiled the Tent of the Lord; that soul shall be wiped out from Israel. Because water of sprinkling was not sprinkled upon him, he is unclean; his uncleanness is still in him.

retained_full_triples.relationship: uncleanness transmitted by an unclean person's touch
retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai's priests affirm that what a corpse-defiled person touches is defiled; Numbers explicitly says whatever the unclean person touches becomes unclean. This is the contact rule applied in Haggai's question.
retained_full_triples.source_text: Haggai said, “If one defiled through a dead person touches any of these, will it be defiled?” The priests answered, “It will be defiled.”

target_units.text: And whatever the unclean person touches shall be unclean, and the person who touches it shall be unclean until evening.

retained_full_triples.relationship: hatred of rebuke at the gates
retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai's expanded native reproof says the people hated those rebuking at the gates; Amos says they hated one reproving at the gates. The unusually particular phrase connects the two rebukes without omitting Haggai's wider defilement application.
retained_full_triples.source_text: Haggai answered, “So is this people, and so is this nation before Me, says the Lord; so are all the works of their hands, and whoever approaches there will be defiled because of their morning gains. They will suffer because of their labors, and you hated those who rebuked at the gates.

target_units.text: They hated one who reproved at the gates and abhorred a holy word.

retained_full_triples.relationship: same-chapter contrast between reflection before and from the rebuilding turning point
retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai first asks the people to set their hearts on the time before stone was placed in the sanctuary; the later instruction asks attention from the stated day and the sanctuary's founding onward. The paired directions structure the before-and-after reflection.
retained_full_triples.source_text: And now, please set your hearts on the time before this day, before stone was placed upon stone in the sanctuary of the Lord,

target_units.text: Please direct your hearts from this day onward; from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month and from the day the sanctuary of the Lord was founded, put it in your hearts:

retained_full_triples.relationship: same-book concrete illustration of reduced agricultural return
retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai's reduced barley and wine measures specify the earlier complaint that much was sown but little brought in. The numerical shortfalls make the earlier agricultural futility concrete without changing the native units of measure.
retained_full_triples.source_text: on how things were with you: when you put twenty sata of barley into a bin, there were ten sata of barley; when you went to the wine vat to draw fifty metretai, there were twenty.

target_units.text: You sowed much and brought in little; you ate, but were not satisfied; you drank, but not to intoxication; you clothed yourselves, but were not warmed in them. The one gathering wages gathered them into a bundle with holes.

retained_full_triples.relationship: divine agricultural blows failing to produce return
retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai says God struck the people's labor with barrenness, wind damage and hail, yet they did not turn to Him; Amos describes burning, jaundice and devoured plantings, also followed by failure to turn. The shared rebuke concerns unheeded discipline, not identical agents of crop damage.
retained_full_triples.source_text: I struck you with barrenness, damage from wind and hail—all the works of your hands—and you did not turn to Me, says the Lord.

target_units.text: “I struck you with burning and jaundice. You multiplied your gardens; the caterpillar devoured your vineyards, fig orchards and olive groves, yet not even so did you turn to Me,” says the Lord.

retained_full_triples.relationship: the temple foundation as a prophetic point of reference
retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai directs attention from the sanctuary's founding and the named day; Zechariah addresses those hearing prophetic words from the day the Lord's house was founded. Both use the foundation as a reference point for the rebuilding community's response.
retained_full_triples.source_text: Please direct your hearts from this day onward; from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month and from the day the sanctuary of the Lord was founded, put it in your hearts:

target_units.text: Thus says the Lord Almighty: Let your hands be strong, you who hear these words in these days from the prophets’ mouth, from the day when the house of the Lord Almighty was founded, and from when the temple was built.

retained_full_triples.relationship: blessing replacing the former lack of agricultural fruit
retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai asks about the still-unfruitful plantings and promises blessing from this day; Zechariah contrasts former treatment of the remnant with vine fruit, earth's produce and blessing. Both place renewed fruitfulness within a reversal from earlier want.
retained_full_triples.source_text: whether it will yet be recognized on the threshing floor, and whether the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate and the olive trees still bear no fruit. From this day I will bless.”

target_units.text: Now I do not act toward this people’s remnant as in the former days, says the Lord Almighty,
but I will show peace: the vine will give its fruit, the earth its produce, and heaven its dew. I will give My people’s remnant all these as an inheritance.
As you were under a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will preserve you, and you will be in blessing. Take courage and be strong in your hands.

retained_full_triples.relationship: same-chapter second revelation on the earlier stated day
retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai calls this a second word on the twenty-fourth day; the earlier heading specifies the twenty-fourth day of month nine in Darius's second year. The headings link the successive law-and-blessing and Zerubbabel messages within the chapter's dated sequence.
retained_full_triples.source_text: The word of the Lord came a second time to Haggai the prophet on the twenty-fourth day of the month, saying:

target_units.text: On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year under Darius, the word of the Lord came to Haggai the prophet, saying:

retained_full_triples.relationship: same-book repetition of the shaking announcement in the word to Zerubbabel
retained_full_triples.rationale: The renewed word to Zerubbabel repeats the shaking of heaven, earth, sea and dry land announced earlier to the rebuilding community. The repeated fourfold scope joins the final oracle to the earlier promise.
retained_full_triples.source_text: “Speak to Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, from the tribe of Judah, saying: I am shaking heaven and earth, the sea and the dry land,

target_units.text: For thus says the Lord Almighty: Once more I will shake heaven and earth, the sea and the dry land.

retained_full_triples.relationship: judgment in which a man's sword turns against his brother
retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai says riders will fall with each one's sword against his brother; Ezekiel announces a man's sword against his brother as part of God's judgment. The precise fraternal combat image supports the parallel without equating the armies.
retained_full_triples.source_text: and I will overturn the thrones of kings and destroy the strength of the kings of the nations. I will overturn chariots and riders; horses and their riders will fall, each with a sword against his brother.

target_units.text: I will summon every fear against him, says the Lord. A man’s sword will be against his brother.

retained_full_triples.relationship: God's sovereignty over the removal of kings
retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai promises to overturn royal thrones and destroy kings' strength; Daniel says God transfers kings and appoints them. Both place royal power under God's authority to remove it.
retained_full_triples.source_text: and I will overturn the thrones of kings and destroy the strength of the kings of the nations. I will overturn chariots and riders; horses and their riders will fall, each with a sword against his brother.

target_units.text: He changes seasons and times, transfers kings and appoints them, gives wisdom to the wise and understanding to those who possess knowledge,

retained_full_triples.relationship: contrasting treatment of a named Judean figure through signet imagery
retained_full_triples.rationale: Haggai promises to make the chosen servant Zerubbabel like a signet; Jeremiah says Jeconiah would be pulled off even if he became a signet on God's right hand. The shared signet image is used for selection in one and removal in the other, without resolving all dynastic implications.
retained_full_triples.source_text: On that day, says the Lord Almighty, I will take you, Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, My servant, says the Lord, and make you like a signet, for I have chosen you, says the Lord Almighty.”

target_units.text: As I live, says the Lord, even if Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, becomes a signet on My right hand, I will pull you off from there,

deferred_source_units.source_text: In the seventh month, on the twenty-first day of the month, the Lord spoke through Haggai the prophet, saying:
deferred_source_units.reason: The complete date heading, the twenty-first day of month seven, was read in its native order. No sufficiently particular parallel for this dated message was established; a generic revelation heading is not counted as a supported connection.

unresolved_candidates.source_text: In the seventh month, on the twenty-first day of the month, the Lord spoke through Haggai the prophet, saying:
unresolved_candidates.reason: Ezra supplies Darius's second year as the end of suspended temple work but does not identify the seventh month's twenty-first day given in this source unit. The broad rebuilding chronology was not retained as a distinct match for this date heading.

target_units.text: Then the work of the house of God in Jerusalem ceased, and it remained idle until the second year of the reign of Darius king of the Persians.
